summary.headline: Aditya Vision Q4 FY26 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR625 crore and PAT 36% to INR22 crore, despite a weak summer and FY26 PAT up only 11%.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue grew 18% to INR2,672 crore and PAT grew 11% to INR117 crore, with EBITDA at INR228 crore (8.5% margin) and gross margin at 15.6%. Q4 was the strongest quarter, with revenue up 28% and same-store sales growth of 18%, though gross margin (16%) and EBITDA margin (8.1%) were lower than the prior year. Management said H2 is now as important as H1, reflecting a shift away from a seasonal model. Store count reached 207 across four states, with Chhattisgarh entered and Madhya Pradesh planned this year. Inventory was built up to about INR840 crore ahead of anticipated OEM supply constraints and BEE-driven price increases.

segments.name: Bihar
segments.commentary: Largest market at 74% of Q4 FY26 revenue and 75% of FY26 revenue; 118 stores across 38 districts.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: 14% of Q4 and 13% of FY26 revenue; 53 stores covering 30 of 75 districts, with most new stores opened in Feb-Mar 2026 and contributing less than a full year.

segments.name: Jharkhand
segments.commentary: 12% of both Q4 and FY26 revenue; 33 stores covering 22 of 24 districts.

segments.name: Chhattisgarh
segments.commentary: Entered early with 3 stores covering 2 of 33 districts; no revenue split disclosed.

segments.name: Product categories
segments.commentary: Mobiles and laptops together exceed 25% of sales; ASP of mobiles rose about 20% in Q4, diluting gross margin. Small appliances grew about 50%, per analyst; cooling products (ACs, coolers, refrigerators) underperformed due to weak summer.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no formal store guidance; it cites about 25 stores when asked, and has added over 30 stores a year for the last 3-5 years.
Madhya Pradesh entry is on track for this financial year; Chhattisgarh and UP to be scaled up.
Management expects opex to grow in line with overall expenses rather than rise faster, as the store base becomes more mature.
Management cites an 8% to 10% EBITDA margin range as its endeavour, with 9% as a central target, but declined to give a timeline.
April 2026 described as very robust; May started colder but is expected to normalise into a normal summer.
No equity raise planned this financial year; internal accruals and working capital borrowings are expected to suffice.
capex_capacity: Store base reached 207 at March 31, 2026, after 102 stores were added in the last three years versus 105 in the prior 23-24 years.
Stores take 9 to 12 months to break even, per management.
Inventory of about INR840 crore held at end Q4 FY26, built ahead of OEM supply uncertainty (gas shortages linked to a Gulf conflict) and BEE-driven price increases of about 8% to 10%.
Plans to scale UP and Chhattisgarh while deepening Bihar and Jharkhand; a neighbouring state, previously held back by political uncertainty, is now being considered.
demand_pricing: Weak summer and extended rains hit H1; Q1 FY26 revenue grew 6% and H1 grew 11%. Q3 grew 28%, driven by festive demand.
Historically Q1 and Q2 contributed 55% to 60% of annual sales; management says this is now shifting towards a more balanced full-year model.
Price increases on mobiles and laptops lowered the margin mix; management said price hikes are not the main driver of profitability.
Management said OEMs bear the burden of unsold inventory and do not take returns; they help liquidate stock before new billing.
Real estate slowdown seen in Pune, Bengaluru and Hyderabad has not yet affected Bihar, UP or Jharkhand, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will high inventory give a competitive and margin advantage over peers in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on peers' inventory and said it holds inventory as per its own strategy and historical levels, not to profit from price hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall about 100 bps YoY in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to weak cooling-product sales in H1 and a Q4 surge in low-margin mobiles (ASP up about 20%) and laptops (ASP up 8-10%), which together exceed 25% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 50% rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to brand ambassador onboarding, UP expansion, and variable costs such as freight, card commissions and dealer discounts that rise with the 18% volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the normalised margins for mature Bihar, and when will UP match them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose state-wise margins, saying it aims to bring other states up to Bihar's level over time without sacrificing sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store expansion target for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance given; management cited 25 stores when pressed and said it expects to keep beating its informal targets.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margin return to about 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no timeline and pointed to an 8% to 10% margin range, with 9% as the central target, while not compromising sales growth.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from mix shift toward mobiles and laptops, whose ASPs are rising.
Q4 inventory build (about INR840 crore) exposes the company to price-cut and demand risk if the summer underperforms; May started colder than normal.
Cash conversion: management declined to guide on OCF/EBITDA, saying it depends on inventory and working capital.
Finance cost implies about 12.8-13% on average debt per analyst, but this includes lease liability interest; the bank borrowing rate was not disclosed.
Most UP stores opened in the last months of FY26, so UP contribution and unit economics are not yet visible on a full-year basis.
Opex rising faster than revenue in new geographies (UP, Chhattisgarh, MP) could weigh on EBITDA margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, demand momentum and the all-season model, but evasive on specifics: management declined to disclose state-wise margins, peer inventory, store targets, cash flow guidance and margin timelines.
key_quotes: I'm truly delighted to give the comfort to our investors and stakeholders that your company is now an all-weather, all-season company.
We do not give a guidance because we are always ahead of the guidance.
So it's not necessary that whenever there is a hike in price that comes as a profit to us.
I cannot give you a guidance on that. But our endeavor, we always give a guidance of between 8% to 10% of margin.
